frozen_at: 2026-09-26, before any scored pilot call (smoke runs on T0 only)
question: On two prespecified small tasks with sealed deterministic oracles, how do v3 prose (P), frozen v2 (V), a strong single agent (S) and best-of-N with the same checks (B) compare at an equal model-call ceiling? Feasibility/case-comparison pilot, not a superiority study (n=1 per cell).
model: claude-opus-5-5 for every role in every arm (one model family; disclosed; no strongest-model privilege)
cap_derivation: 1.25 x max(complete smoke paths on T0): V 33 calls (smoke-V-T0), P 39 calls (smoke-P-T0) -> 48.75 -> 49

arms.S: one agent, same workspace/tools/public checks; up to 12 revise-and-check cycles (cap/4); 1 model context
arms.B: 24 independent fresh revisions of v0 (cap/2), each + 1 Verifier call on source criteria; select by public checks pass, then fewest verifier flags, then fewer words, then index; no judges
arms.V: frozen v2 (commit 24663bd) SKILL.md + INITIATOR.md, orchestrator-in-the-loop relay (harness re-invokes the orchestrator each step; roles run as fresh subagents)
arms.P: final v3 SKILL.md + INITIATOR.md (hash appended as amendment 3 before P runs), same relay; no rqgm_check.py in the workspace

runs: one per arm x task (8); launched concurrently; memory reset (fresh workspace per run)
human_proxy: sealed/pilot-heldout-and-proxy.md (escalate when offered; never amend/waive/close [OPEN]; newer at oscillation; held-out = 3 per-task prompts, majority, failing IDs only)

endpoints.primary: sealed score.py required_all_pass on the final emitted artifact (B: the selected candidate)
endpoints.false_completion: arm claims DONE/COMPLETE but required_all_pass is false
secondary: process coverage and archive audit (P and V with rqgm_check.py where format allows)

decision_rule: Report paired case outcomes and costs without significance claims. P may be called better on these cases under these ceilings only if its correctness/cost results justify that restricted statement against both V and the simple comparators (S, B); mixed or equal results are inconclusive. (peer_review_rqgm_v2.md 4.4)
contamination: sealed files live outside every workspace; subagents are told not to read outside it; post-hoc grep of all journals for sealed paths
limitations: one model family for all roles and judges
per-step orchestrator re-invocation differs from a live session
T2 was co-designed with the v3 effort (planted unknown + causal claim favour fail-closed rules)
sealed files have no technical access boundary
S's internal turns are not counted as calls; compare tokens
answer keys and held-out prompts written by the orchestrating Claude session, not a human
